correctness.rationale: The common-reset coupling gives exponential convergence and uniqueness; stationary age is Exp(r), and the independent conditional Gaussian innovations give H_i=(D_i/2)(1−e^(−ω_i A))Z_i². Distinct-label subset moments reduce to moments of the conditional means, unlike moments with repeated indices. The exponential-age transform gives strictly positive pair covariance and factors the triple cumulant into a strictly positive multiplier times 2r³+2sr²−(sp−q). I reproduced the symbolic factorization through the stationary generator on products of normalized energies: (r+Σ_{i∈I}ω_i)M_I=Σ_{i∈I}ω_i M_{I∖{i}}. The constant sp−q=(a+b)(a+c)(b+c)>0 and the cubic is strictly increasing for r>0. At fixed s, log(sp−q)=Σ_i log(s−ω_i) is strictly Schur-concave, and the root increases with sp−q. At equality r*=s/3. If m is the smallest rate, sp−q >= 4m²(s−m)>2m²(s+m) unless all rates coincide, proving the strict lower bound. Energy is coordinatewise increasing in the independent age and Gaussian squares, so product-measure association, then truncation, applies to square-integrable increasing observables. The example (1,2,3) gives 1.943380912562617.
residual_risks: Strict Schur ordering compares triples by majorization at fixed sum, not every pair of unequal triples. Parameters must be positive; the statement is about distinct labels under full common resetting, and neither repeated energies nor partial resets follow.

value.rationale: The result separates positive pair dependence and even association from the sign of a connected three-mode statistic. It gives an explicit parameter-uniform boundary and shows how balancing independently confined modes moves it at fixed sum. This is a useful diagnostic in a common-environment model, beyond computing a raw third moment or reusing the homogeneous beta law.
residual_risks: This is a statistical sign boundary, not a thermodynamic phase transition. There is no inference guarantee for data or general ordering for other reset mechanisms.
